prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: Naive Bayes Classifier
area.rationale: Naive Bayes theory, variants, probability foundations, independence assumption, smoothing, log-trick, training, and implementation.

candidates.label: Naive Bayes Classifier Core
candidates.description: Naive Bayes is a probabilistic classifier that applies Bayes' theorem with the naive assumption of feature independence given the class. It computes posterior probability for each class and predicts the one with maximum probability.
coverage_criteria: State the naive independence assumption.
Describe how Naive Bayes uses Bayes theorem for classification.
Identify that it is an eager learning algorithm.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Probability Foundations for Naive Bayes
candidates.description: Foundational probability concepts: basic probability, conditional probability P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B), and Bayes theorem P(B|A) = P(A|B)P(B)/P(A) with posterior, likelihood, prior, and evidence.
coverage_criteria: State the formula for conditional probability.
Write Bayes theorem and name the terms.
Compute a simple probability using the formula.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Feature Independence Assumption and Multicollinearity
candidates.description: Naive Bayes assumes features are independent given the class (the 'naive' assumption). Multicollinearity (high feature correlation) violates this independence, causing poor performance.
coverage_criteria: Explain the naive independence assumption.
Define multicollinearity and its impact on Naive Bayes.
Describe a method to detect multicollinearity.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Naive Bayes Variants: Bernoulli, Multinomial, Gaussian
candidates.description: Three main variants: Bernoulli for binary features, Multinomial for discrete counts (especially text), and Gaussian for continuous features assuming a normal distribution.
coverage_criteria: Match each variant to its typical data type.
Identify the appropriate variant for a given scenario.
Recognize scikit-learn class names for each variant.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Zero Frequency Error and Laplace Smoothing
candidates.description: Zero frequency error occurs when a test feature value was not seen during training, causing zero posterior probability. Laplace smoothing adds a small constant (usually 1) to counts to avoid zeros.
coverage_criteria: Define zero frequency error.
Explain how Laplace smoothing mitigates the error.
Describe the effect of the smoothing parameter α.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Practical Aspects of Naive Bayes: Applications, Advantages, and Usage
candidates.description: Naive Bayes is used in text classification, sentiment analysis, recommendation, and real-time prediction. Advantages: fast, less training data (when independent), good with categorical/text data. Disadvantages: independence assumption, zero frequency. Best when features are fairly independent and for text tasks.
coverage_criteria: List at least three real-world applications.
State two advantages and two disadvantages.
Describe scenarios where Naive Bayes is a good choice or should be avoided.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Improving Naive Bayes Performance
candidates.description: Techniques include removing correlated features, feature engineering, domain knowledge, using probabilistic features, Laplace smoothing, and the log-trick for numerical stability: argmax (log prior + Σ log P(xᵢ|y)).
coverage_criteria: Name at least three improvement strategies.
Explain why the log-trick is used.
Apply the log-trick in a posterior calculation.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Gaussian Naive Bayes: Prior, Likelihood, and PDF
candidates.description: In Gaussian Naive Bayes, the prior P(y) is the class frequency. The class conditional probability P(xᵢ|y) is modeled with a Gaussian PDF: (1/√(2πσ²)) exp(-(x-μ)²/(2σ²)), where μ and σ² are estimated per feature per class.
coverage_criteria: Calculate prior probabilities from a dataset.
Write the Gaussian PDF formula.
Compute a PDF value given mean and variance.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Naive Bayes Training and Prediction Procedure
candidates.description: Training: compute per-class means, variances, and prior probabilities. Prediction: choose the class with the highest log-posterior: log P(y) + Σ log P(xᵢ|y) using argmax.
coverage_criteria: List the statistics computed during training.
Explain the prediction step using argmax.
Perform a simple prediction by hand for a small dataset.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Implementing Naive Bayes in Python
candidates.description: The classifier is implemented as a Python class with fit() and predict() methods, using NumPy arrays, storing learned parameters as attributes. Model performance is evaluated using accuracy on a test set.
coverage_criteria: Describe the class structure and key methods (fit, predict).
Explain how accuracy is computed and interpreted.
Identify the attributes stored after training (e.g., means, variances, priors).
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Sentiment Analysis: Definition and Supervised Learning
candidates.description: Sentiment analysis classifies text as positive or negative based on sentiment-bearing words. It is a supervised classification task that requires labeled data for training.
coverage_criteria: Define sentiment analysis.
Explain why labeled data is necessary for supervised sentiment analysis.
Give examples of positive and negative cue words.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Derivation of Naive Bayes Decision Rule
candidates.description: The step-by-step derivation from Bayes theorem to the final classification formula: select class c that maximizes P(c) * ∏ P(word|c).
coverage_criteria: Write the final decision rule formula.
Explain the steps: posterior maximization, dropping the denominator, independence assumption.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Naive Bayes Training: Prior and Likelihood Computation
candidates.description: How to compute prior class probabilities P(c) = Nc/N and word likelihoods P(word|c) as relative frequency in class c.
coverage_criteria: Calculate prior from class counts.
Calculate word likelihoods from training documents.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Laplace Smoothing in Naive Bayes
candidates.description: Adding a constant (usually 1) to all word counts to avoid zero probabilities for unseen words, using the formula (count + 1) / (total words + vocabulary size).
coverage_criteria: Explain the zero probability problem.
Apply Laplace smoothing to word count tables.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Logarithmic Transformation for Numerical Stability
candidates.description: Using the log of the Naive Bayes product to convert it into a sum, preventing underflow from multiplying many small probabilities.
coverage_criteria: Explain why log-sum avoids underflow.
Transform a product expression into a log-sum.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Stemming
candidates.description: Reducing words to their root form (e.g., 'running' → 'run') to consolidate terms, using algorithms like SnowballStemmer from NLTK.
coverage_criteria: Explain the purpose of stemming.
Apply a stemmer to a list of words.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Binary Multinomial Naive Bayes
candidates.description: A variant that uses binary features (word presence/absence) instead of word counts, emphasizing occurrence over frequency.
coverage_criteria: Contrast binary and frequency-based Naive Bayes.
Explain when binary features might be useful.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Fundamentos do Naive Bayes
candidates.description: Compreensão do teorema de Bayes, da suposição de independência ingênua, e como eles formam a base do classificador Naive Bayes para classificação de texto.
coverage_criteria: Enunciar o teorema de Bayes e aplicá-lo à classificação.
Explicar a suposição de independência e sua implicação na fatoração de P(X|y).
Calcular a probabilidade de classe dado um exemplo a partir de frequências de termos.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Aplicação do Multinomial Naive Bayes em scikit-learn
candidates.description: Implementação prática do classificador MultinomialNB para análise de sentimento ou detecção de spam, incluindo preparação dos dados e treinamento.
coverage_criteria: Justificar a escolha do MultinomialNB para dados de contagem de palavras.
Carregar e pré-processar um dataset de texto para classificação.
Treinar um modelo MultinomialNB e fazer predições.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Divisão treino-teste para avaliação de modelos
candidates.description: Particionamento dos dados em conjuntos de treino e teste para avaliar a generalização do modelo e detectar overfitting.
coverage_criteria: Explicar a necessidade de separar os dados.
Utilizar train_test_split do scikit-learn.
Discutir o que ocorre se não houver divisão (overfitting).
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Métricas de avaliação para classificação
candidates.description: Métricas derivadas da matriz de confusão: acurácia, precisão, recall, F1-score, para avaliar o desempenho de classificadores binários.
coverage_criteria: Definir matriz de confusão e os termos VP, FP, VN, FN.
Calcular acurácia, precisão, recall e F1-score a partir da matriz.
Interpretar o significado de cada métrica.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Ajuste de hiperparâmetros com GridSearchCV
candidates.description: Busca exaustiva dos melhores hiperparâmetros usando validação cruzada para otimizar o desempenho do classificador Naive Bayes.
coverage_criteria: Explicar o propósito do ajuste de hiperparâmetros.
Diferenciar Grid Search de Random Search.
Aplicar GridSearchCV no scikit-learn para encontrar os melhores parâmetros.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Distribuição de classes desbalanceada
candidates.description: Identificação de conjuntos de dados com desproporção entre classes e compreensão de seu impacto na classificação.
coverage_criteria: Reconhecer um dataset desbalanceado a partir da distribuição de rótulos.
Discutir por que dados desbalanceados podem ser problemáticos.
Mencionar possíveis estratégias de mitigação.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
